title: Taylor Digital Food Scale not Big on Intuition, but Acceptable
text:
Taylor Digital Food Scale not Big on Intuition, but Acceptable. Those who are serious about dieting often consider a food scale an essential part of the weight management process and the Taylor scale is a handy little tool for this purpose. It checks a food's weight, matches it to the type of food, and then delivers a calculation for total calories, helping dieters and others control food intake and keep calories in check.

This scale takes a little effort to set up. The battery compartment uses watch- style batteries and it has to be opened with a very small screwdriver. It would be better, and easier, if the compartment could be opened without a screwdriver and I would like it better if it used ordinary batteries, but the setup process was acceptable at this point and I was now ready to use the scale. The manufacturer says that 1000 food items are already pre- loaded into the scale, so in most instances, it is just a matter of finding your food item in the database, placing it on the scale, and waiting for the display to show the total calories. If you have a food that is not in the database, you can add it manually, into the scale's memory, for future reference.

The Taylor scale is a useful device for checking food weight and caloric values, but I must say that it isn't the most intuitive when it comes to programming and food lookup. As I said before, you can input your own food items manually, but it takes time because all you have is a 10- key keypad, similar to a standard phone. You have to press the numbered key containing the desired letter either once, twice, or three times depending on its position on the button. This can take some time, depending on the word. Then, you have to be ready to input the number of calories in a 100 gram serving. It is a good idea to have a calculator handy for this purpose.

Serious dieters will enjoy this scale the best, but others can benefit from it as well. We could all use a little better diet management and this Taylor scale does come in handy for this purpose. It could use a little more intuition and perhaps a few more bells and whistles, as well as larger keys, but it is still a good starter unit that has the basics covered.

product_metadata.title: Taylor Cal-Max Digital Food Scale with Calorie Calculator
features: Measures calories in 1000 dry and liquid foods
Memory function for multiple meal tracking
Measures calories by the weight of the food
Kitchen scale as well as a calorie scale
description: The same Cal-Max technology that we have in our bath scales. The weight of the item determines the calories in over 1000 different foods and liquids. Easy to use food look up makes tracking calories a lot easier. The easy to read LCD readout is easy to see in all lighting conditions.Measure the food in your own container or on the easy to clean scale surface.
